heroDescription: Founded in 1994, The Association of Bow Valley Area Rockclimbers is a 100% volunteer-run registered non-profit dedicated to funding fixed hardware, anchors, and crag maintenance throughout the Canadian Rockies.

mandateCards.title: Fixed Hardware Funding
mandateCards.description: Raising and distributing funds to cover material costs for stainless steel expansion bolts, AustriAlpin glue-in anchors, and chains installed by active route builders.

mandateCards.title: Retrofitting & Safety Upgrades
mandateCards.description: Incentivizing the replacement of aging 1980s and 1990s plated hardware with zero funding caps for safety retrofits on established climbs.

mandateCards.title: 100% Volunteer Driven
mandateCards.description: Over $180,000 raised and distributed. With no salaries or offices, your donations go directly into equipment on the rock face.

retroboltingCaption: TABVAR volunteers and active route developers collaborating on anchor upgrades in Grotto Canyon.
memorialBio: Jon Jones was the president of TABVAR from its founding in 1994 until his retirement in 2020. His relentless dedication to both fundraising and pioneering route development was the primary engine behind the Bow Valley becoming a vibrant, world-renowned climbing destination.

While best known for hundreds of modern sport routes, there is no shortage of bold, classic multipitches bearing his name. Jon was meticulous, detail-oriented, and passionately committed to steadily elevating the safety and installation standards of Bow Valley climbing.
clinicCaption: TABVAR Volunteer Leadership & Routebuilder Community: Board directors and Bow Valley developers gather annually to align on modern glue-in bolting, torque mechanics, and crag conservation.
